title: Finite filtration of a finitely generated subsheaf of the constant sheaf
statement: Let X be a topological space in which the intersection of any two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact. Let K be a subsheaf of the constant abelian sheaf \underline{\mathbf Z}_X [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] generated by finitely many sections over quasi-compact opens. Then K has a finite filtration 0=K_0 \subset K_1 \subset \cdots \subset K_n=K such that each successive quotient K_i/K_{i-1} fits into a short exact sequence 0 \to j'_! \underline{\mathbf Z}_V \to j_! \underline{\mathbf Z}_U \to K_i/K_{i-1} \to 0 for quasi-compact opens V and U of X and their open immersions j',j, where j'_! and j_! are extension by zero [lem-sc-topological-extension-by-zero-stalks].

proof.text: Write K as generated by sections s_i on quasi-compact opens U_i. A locally constant integer-valued section on a quasi-compact open has finitely many clopen fibres, so after replacing each U_i by those finitely many clopen pieces we may assume s_i is the constant integer n_i. Delete zero generators and change signs so n_i>0. For every subset I of the finite index set, adjoin the pair (intersection of the U_i, gcd of the n_i); intersections remain quasi-compact by hypothesis, and adjoining these pairs does not change the generated subsheaf because the gcd is an integral linear combination of the n_i and conversely divides each n_i. Thus, at every point x, the gcd of the integers attached to generators whose opens contain x is one of the attached integers.

For every integer r\ge 0 let K_r be the subsheaf generated by the generators with n_i\le r (so K_0=0); this is an increasing filtration which is constant, equal to K, for r\ge\max n_i. Put U_r=\bigcup_{n_i\le r}U_i, V_r=\bigcup_{n_i<r}U_i and W_r=\bigcup_{n_i=r}U_i, finite unions of quasi-compact opens, hence quasi-compact, with V_r\subseteq U_r=V_r\cup W_r. Stalks: since the stalk of a subsheaf generated by sections is the subgroup generated by their germs, (K_r)_x=g\mathbf Z with g the gcd of the n_i, i\in I_x, n_i\le r. The intersection of these U_i with that gcd was adjoined in Step 1 and has value \le r, so g itself is the value of a generator with n_i\le r through x. Hence for x\in V_r we get (K_r)_x=(K_{r-1})_x: otherwise g=r, but r would then divide some n_i<r with x\in U_i. For x\in U_r\setminus V_r every generator through x of value \le r has value r, so (K_r)_x=r\mathbf Z and (K_{r-1})_x=0. For x\notin U_r both stalks are 0. Thus the quotient K_r/K_{r-1} has zero stalks on V_r, so the class of the constant section r of K_r on W_r and the zero section on V_r agree on W_r\cap V_r and glue to a section \sigma_r of K_r/K_{r-1} over U_r which generates it (the quotient is generated by the classes of the sections n_i=r on the U_i with n_i=r). Note that the integer r itself need not be a section of K_r over U_r (e.g. values 2 and 3 on disjoint opens), which is why \sigma_r is defined by gluing.

The section \sigma_r of Step 2 defines a morphism \beta\colon j_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_{U_r}\to K_r/K_{r-1} sending 1 to \sigma_r, and the inclusion V_r\subseteq U_r defines \alpha\colon j'_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_{V_r}\to j_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_{U_r}; both are induced by the defining presheaf maps for extension by zero, and \beta\circ\alpha=0 because \sigma_r vanishes on V_r. Compute stalks with [lem-sc-topological-extension-by-zero-stalks] and the stalks of Step 2. If x\notin U_r, all three stalks are 0. If x\in U_r\setminus V_r, then (j'_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_{V_r})_x=0 and \beta_x\colon\mathbf Z\to(K_r/K_{r-1})_x=r\mathbf Z sends 1 to r, an isomorphism. If x\in V_r, then \alpha_x\colon\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z is the identity and (K_r/K_{r-1})_x=0. Thus 0\to(j'_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_{V_r})_x\to(j_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_{U_r})_x\to(K_r/K_{r-1})_x\to 0 is exact for every x, and the stalkwise short-exactness criterion [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-short-exact-stalkwise] gives the short exact sequence 0\to j'_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_{V_r}\to j_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_{U_r}\to K_r/K_{r-1}\to 0.

Delete the indices r with K_r=K_{r-1} (for these the quotient is 0 and the sequence above is trivial) and relabel the remaining stages as K_1,\dots,K_n. Then 0=K_0\subset K_1\subset\cdots\subset K_n=K is the required finite filtration, and each successive quotient fits into the short exact sequence of Step 3 with the quasi-compact opens U_r, V_r and their open inclusions j, j'.
